invariants.name: Admission requires a passed positive run, the expected negative run and a passed restored run
A failed run stops the proof
A proof with a base ref reads its diff from the merge base
An admitted proof has a manifest base that is an ancestor of the diff target

carrier.contract: runModel writes only its own temp root and removes it when the run ends or a stop kills it. Each judge maps one RunEnd to a Result and writes nothing.

category.equality: Two run ends are equal when their kind and fields are equal. Two judged results are equal when their counts, violation or refusal text are equal.

abstraction.hides: The start of three TLC processes at once, the kill of the live runs after a stop, and the wait for the cleanup of each temp root.
callersKnow: check proof judges the runs in the order positive, negative, restored, so its first stop is the same as in a run in sequence.
A stop kills the runs that are still live and removes each temp root before the command exits.
A local run of scripts/check-proof.ts reads origin/HEAD and passes HEAD^ or origin/<default> as its base.
With no origin/HEAD that resolves, or no HEAD^, the local run keeps the manifest base.
abstraction.deletionTest: Deleting stopRuns puts the abort and the cleanup wait at each stop of prove, so one stop can return while a run still owns a temp root.

alternatives.name: Runs in sequence
alternatives.rejectedBecause: Three runs in sequence took 8.0 s on this tree, and together they took 3.5 s.

alternatives.name: A wait for all three runs
alternatives.rejectedBecause: A fast positive failure waits for the slowest run, up to the 60 s deadline.

alternatives.name: A stop at the first run to end
alternatives.rejectedBecause: A wrong negative that ends first can hide the positive failure, so the first stop can change.

omitted: The processes, their start order and the kill signal are abstracted to one judged result for each run.
The model sees the judged results in the order positive, negative, restored, and not the order in which the runs end.
Git, origin/HEAD and the merge base algorithm are abstracted to one base observation for each run.
The launcher, the node floor and check:fast are not in the model. Their tests and the gates examine them.

bounds: One base observation for each run from 48 cases: four relations, a ref or none, two diff bases, two history views and an authority move that needs a ref.
The authority cases, five validation stages and the bounded positive, negative, restored and freshness results of the earlier model.
Finite Result laws use two values, two errors and all total functions between them.

negative.defect: Dropping the restored check admits a proof whose restored run did not pass, as a judge that stops after the first two runs would.

limits: The finite model takes each judged run result as true. It does not model processes, signals or temp roots. The CP-02 and CP-10 controls examine them.
The model does not check the launcher, the node floor, check:fast or the CI trigger. Their tests, check:drift and the CI step examine them.
The model does not check the words of the docs and the ADR notes. Review and the STE, chart, budget and drift gates examine them.
Exact-head CI, review and every ordinary gate stay required.
